# Replacing each command in an action combinatorially is what proves every
# input is coupled to a failure, but n inputs need 2^n-1 cases and each case
# is a full test run. --max-cases bounds that.
#
# An action over the bound is not quietly dropped. It is reported where its
# mutants would have been, with the arithmetic that ruled it out, so a run
# that skipped work says so instead of looking thorough.
#
# Here the action reads two inputs, .First and .Last, so it needs three cases.
# Under a bound of two it is skipped; raised to four, all three are tried.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1 --max-cases 2
cmp stdout want-skipped.txt

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1 --max-cases 4
cmp stdout want-enumerated.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "greeting"}}{{printf "%s %s" .First .Last}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	First string
	Last  string
}

func Greet(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreet(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Greet(&buf, Page{First: "Ada", Last: "Lovelace"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Ada Lovelace"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want-skipped.txt --

    KILL 1:22 action-zero
    SKIP 1:22 operands (2 operands need 3 cases, over --max-cases=2)
